title: Evacuated Residents from Russian-Occupied Oleshky Cross Into Ukraine

meta_description: Civilians evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have crossed into Ukrainian-held territory under a U.S.-brokered temporary ceasefire.
discover_titles: Evacuated Residents Return to Ukraine After U.S.-Brokered Ceasefire
Oleshky Evacuees Cross Into Ukrainian Territory From Belarus
Humanitarian Mission Brings Oleshky Residents Back to Ukraine
spot: Residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky as part of a U.S.-brokered temporary ceasefire crossed back into Ukrainian-held territory on Saturday, following a complex journey through Russia and Belarus.
content_html:
Key Developments

Civilians who were evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian-held territory on Saturday following a deal brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump. The travelers moved by bus and plane through Russia and Belarus as part of a temporary ceasefire agreement that began at 3 a.m. Tuesday and is scheduled to run through Sunday evening.

Oleshky, located in Ukraine's southeastern Kherson region, has been occupied by Russia since the early days of the war, creating one of the conflict's most severe humanitarian crises. The estimated 2,000 remaining residents were given the option to travel to Ukrainian- or Russian-held territory, or remain in the city alongside replenished food and medical supplies.

Those choosing to return to Ukraine traveled first to the Russian city of Anapa, then took a flight to Homel in Belarus before heading to the border. Ukrainian authorities restricted the disclosure of exact evacuee numbers and border crossing locations to protect those remaining in Oleshky and safeguard future humanitarian missions. Relatives, aid tents, coffee stands, pet provisions, and volunteers from organizations such as the Red Cross, Doctors Without Borders, and World Central Kitchen awaited the arrivals at the border.

Key Takeaways

  • U.S.-Brokered Deal: The evacuation was facilitated by a temporary ceasefire brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, running from Tuesday through Sunday evening.
  • Complex Transit Route: Evacuees traveled via buses and planes through Russia (Anapa) and Belarus (Homel) before reaching Ukrainian territory.
  • Humanitarian Options: Remaining residents in Oleshky could choose between relocating to Ukrainian- or Russian-held zones or staying with new food and medical supplies.

Why It Matters

The successful evacuation highlights a rare humanitarian corridor established during the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, offering relief to one of the conflict's most dire localized crises. Oleshky has remained under Russian occupation since the war's initial days, leaving families separated for years. The operation provides emotional reunions for relatives like Liza Paliy and Daria Pavlyn, who have waited years or months to reconnect with loved ones left behind in occupied territory, while also setting a precedent for targeted humanitarian interventions.
